hull.what_it_is: The armoured hull is the primary welded monocoque structural chassis and ballistic envelope of the combat vehicle that houses the crew, powerpack, ammunition, and internal sub-systems.
hull.what_it_does: It provides all-aspect ballistic protection against direct kinetic and chemical threats, absorbs dynamic operational shock from terrain and main gun recoil, and maintains rigid dimensional alignment across the suspension, engine bed, and turret interface plinths.
hull.where_it_fits: Primary Vehicle Chassis and Base Structure.
explicit_relationships: Lower Hull Plate and Glacis Plate are joined via submerged arc / robotic GMAW to form the hull tub envelope.
Turret Ring Plinth is machined directly into the upper deck of the hull tub.
Transverse bulkheads are welded across the lower hull plate to provide lateral stiffness.
hull.general_context_note: The hull's role as the welded armoured chassis tub and its constituent plates and assemblies are directly stated in the Hull Welding SOP; its broader role as the primary vehicle body is general engineering context.

hull plate.what_it_is: Heavy rolled homogeneous armour (RHA) high-hard alloy steel structural plates fabricated according to defense metallurgical specifications.
hull plate.what_it_does: Forms the protective structural boundaries of the vehicle tub, designed to resist high-velocity ballistic impacts and structural deformation.
explicit_relationships: Welded together using multi-pass submerged arc or gas metal arc welding.
Root gaps and preheat temperatures are strictly controlled before joint welding.

lower hull plate.what_it_is: The heavy bottom floor plate of the armoured vehicle tub fabricated from high-strength armoured plate steel.
lower hull plate.what_it_does: Forms the structural floor of the hull, defends against mine and underbody blast energy, and provides foundation mounting points for transverse bulkheads and suspension tube sleeves.
explicit_relationships: Mated to the glacis plate at the frontal nose and to sponson boxes along the lateral flanks.
Tack welded at controlled pitch prior to automated robotic weld passes.

glacis plate.what_it_is: The thick, highly sloped forward armour plate shielding the front of the vehicle hull.
glacis plate.what_it_does: Presents a steeply angled ballistic profile to ricochet and defeat incoming kinetic and shaped-charge projectiles across the vehicle's frontal arc.
explicit_relationships: Welded to the lower hull plate along the frontal transverse nose seam with verified root gap tolerances (2.5 mm ± 0.5 mm in V1, 2.0 mm ± 0.3 mm in V2).
Joined to lateral sponson box plates.

sponson box.what_it_is: The lateral overhanging structural compartments projecting outward from the main hull tub sides over the track runs.
sponson box.what_it_does: Houses electrical wiring looms, fuel cells, air intake filtration ducts, and tools while stiffening the lateral sidewalls of the vehicle hull.
sponson box.where_it_fits: Armoured Hull Tub Assembly (Port and Starboard Sides).
explicit_relationships: Welded directly to the side longitudinal plates of the lower hull tub.
Geometric alignment is verified using coordinate laser metrology.

hull tub assembly.what_it_is: The unified monocoque structural enclosure formed by complete welding of the lower plate, glacis plate, side sponsons, and bulkheads.
hull tub assembly.what_it_does: Acts as the rigid structural core of the entire armored fighting vehicle, supporting all mobility, firepower, and protection assemblies.
explicit_relationships: Integrates the lower hull, glacis, sponsons, and engine bay bulkheads into a sealed armored unit.
Undergoes post-weld stress relief and ultrasonic non-destructive flaw detection.

weld joint.what_it_is: A precision backing strip made from ceramic or sacrificial structural steel positioned behind heavy plate weld joints.
weld joint.what_it_does: Supports the molten weld pool during the high-amperage root pass, preventing burn-through and ensuring 100% root penetration across thick armour bevels.
weld joint.where_it_fits: Armoured Plate Seams (Hull and Structure Joints).
explicit_relationships: Clamped behind the plate root gap prior to preheating and welding.
Removed or ground flush during final post-weld quality inspection.

turret.what_it_is: The rotating armoured fighting structure mounted atop the vehicle hull that encloses the main gun, sighting systems, and crew stations.
turret.what_it_does: Provides 360-degree azimuth fire capability for the main gun and secondary armament while protecting the commander, gunner, and autoloader mechanism.
turret.where_it_fits: Upper Vehicle Structure (mounted to the Hull Plinth via Turret Base Ring).
explicit_relationships: Mated to the hull deck plinth through the turret bearing and retention ring.
Connected electrically to the hull via the central rotary slip ring.
Traversed in azimuth by the dual-pinion anti-backlash drive.
turret.general_context_note: The mechanical and electrical mating of the turret to the hull is directly stated in the Turret Integration SOP; broader combat vehicle roles are general engineering context.

turret base ring.what_it_is: A precision-forged and machined heavy steel annular ring mounted on the vehicle hull's upper deck plinth.
turret base ring.what_it_does: Provides the stationary circular foundation and bearing raceway seat that carries the rotating turret weight and reacts dynamic main gun firing loads.
turret base ring.where_it_fits: Turret Integration System / Hull Upper Deck Interface.
explicit_relationships: Bolted to the hull deck plinth with high-tensile fasteners torqued to 185 Nm (V1) or 210 Nm (V2).
Seats the bearing raceway that supports the rotating turret basket.

turret mount.what_it_is: The integrated mechanical assembly comprising the hull plinth, base ring, bearing raceway, and retention hardware supporting the turret.
turret mount.what_it_does: Secures the turret to the hull, provides low-friction 360-degree rotation, and prevents turret dislodgement under high-angle ballistic impacts or vehicle turnover.
explicit_relationships: Interfaces the hull plinth directly to the turret basket structure.
Secured by the ballistic retention ring with calibrated torque-angle fasteners.

ceramic-hybrid bearing.what_it_is: A heavy-duty precision turret bearing assembly featuring silicon nitride (Si3N4) ceramic rollers alternating between hardened steel raceways.
ceramic-hybrid bearing.what_it_does: Supports the 18-tonne rotating turret basket on the hull plinth, provides high-rigidity rotational motion with minimal friction, prevents electrical microwelding, and resists brinelling under extreme gun recoil shock.
ceramic-hybrid bearing.where_it_fits: Turret Integration System (introduced in Rev 4.5 V2 to replace the Rev 3.8 four-point steel ball bearing).
explicit_relationships: Installed between the stationary turret base ring and the rotating turret basket.
Ceramic rollers feature sphericity grade tolerance within 0.0005 mm.

engine.what_it_is: A 12-cylinder V-configuration turbocharged, liquid-cooled multi-fuel diesel internal combustion engine producing 1000 hp (735 kW).
engine.what_it_does: Generates the prime rotational mechanical power needed to drive the vehicle tracks, auxiliary hydraulic pumps, and onboard electrical generation systems.
engine.where_it_fits: V12 Powerpack Assembly (located in the Rear Hull Engine Bay).
explicit_relationships: Mounted to the hull engine bed via resilient rubber-metal mounts (V1) or active hydromounts (V2).
Directs rotational power through the crankshaft coupling into the transmission gearbox.
engine.general_context_note: Technical alignment tolerances and mount damping are directly stated in the Engine Alignment SOP; general engine operational principles are general engineering context.

v12 powerpack.what_it_is: A unified, quick-disconnect power module integrating the 1000-hp V12 diesel engine, cooling radiators, dry-sump lubrication, turbochargers, and electrical interface.
v12 powerpack.what_it_does: Serves as the complete self-contained vehicular power unit designed for rapid field replacement in under 45 minutes using standard recovery crane hoisting.
v12 powerpack.where_it_fits: Rear Engine Bay Compartment of the Hull.
explicit_relationships: Connected to the transmission input shaft via a dynamically balanced flexible gear coupling.
Secured to the hull floor by four calibrated vibration damping mounts.

torsion bar.what_it_is: A high-strength alloy spring steel cylindrical shaft with precision splined ends that spans transversely across the bottom width of the vehicle hull.
torsion bar.what_it_does: Acts as the primary suspension spring for each road wheel; twists elastically under balancer arm deflection to absorb shock loads and support vehicle sprung weight.
torsion bar.where_it_fits: Torsion Suspension Subsystem (installed inside transverse hull tube stations).
explicit_relationships: Inboard spline anchors into the opposite hull wall anchor plug; outboard spline locks into the balancer arm hub.
Preloaded at an initial preset angle of 32° ± 0.5° before road wheel fitment.

hydromount.what_it_is: An advanced fluid-filled elastomeric vibration isolation mount with electronically or hydraulically tuned fluid damping passages.
hydromount.what_it_does: Isolates the vehicle hull and transmission from engine low-frequency torque pulses and attenuates high-frequency vibration during high-speed tactical cross-country operations.
hydromount.where_it_fits: V12 Powerpack Mounting Interface / Engine Bay Hull Pedestals (introduced in Rev 6.0 V2).
explicit_relationships: Supports the front and rear trunnions of the V12 powerpack in V2.
Maintains cold radial offset within 0.08 mm under thermal expansion.

track.what_it_is: An endless continuous articulated belt consisting of forged steel track shoes linked together by rubber-bushed double pins and end-connectors.
track.what_it_does: Distributes the vehicle's 45+ tonne weight across a broad ground contact area, engages the drive sprocket to propel the vehicle, and guides road wheel motion across obstacle terrain.
explicit_relationships: Driven by teeth on the rear drive sprocket; guided by six pairs of road wheels and front idler.
Static upper track catenary sag is calibrated to 35–45 mm in V1 and 25–35 mm in V2.

suspension.what_it_is: The independent high-travel running gear subsystem comprising transverse torsion bars, balancer arms, needle-bearing housings, road wheel hubs, and dampers.
suspension.what_it_does: Cushions the vehicle against terrain shock, keeps tracks firmly planted on rough soil, and provides stable gun platform dynamics during fire-on-the-move operations.
suspension.where_it_fits: Lower Hull Running Gear (both Port and Starboard Flanks).
explicit_relationships: Transfers ground reaction forces from the road wheels through the balancer arms into the torsion bars.
Damped at extreme wheel stations (stations 1, 2, and 6) by heavy-duty hydraulic or magnetorheological rotary dampers.

bearing raceway.what_it_is: Precision induction-hardened concentric steel rings featuring V-grooved tracks that guide the bearing rolling elements.
bearing raceway.what_it_does: Confines bearing rollers at alternating 90-degree angles to absorb concurrent radial, thrust, and tilting moment loads from the turret.
explicit_relationships: Machined directly into or mounted upon the turret base ring.
Surface raceway hardness is verified at 58–62 HRC.

ceramic rollers.what_it_is: Ultra-hard, precision-ground cylindrical rolling elements manufactured from sintered silicon nitride (Si3N4) ceramic.
ceramic rollers.what_it_does: Rolls within the cross-roller raceway to facilitate turret traverse while eliminating electrical conductivity, resisting corrosion, and preventing galling.
explicit_relationships: Assembled into alternating cross-roller orientation within the V2 turret bearing.
Inspected for sphericity within 0.0005 mm.

needle-bearing housing.what_it_is: A heavy-duty machined outer casing enclosing needle rollers, spacer rings, and multi-lip elastomer grease seals.
needle-bearing housing.what_it_does: Houses the pivot journal of the balancer arm on the outer hull, providing low-friction angular rotation while resisting extreme radial suspension shock.
explicit_relationships: Press-fit into the outer hull suspension station bore.
Sealed by a labyrinth seal (V1) or triple-lip cassette seal (V2) to exclude water and mud.

track system.what_it_is: The track system is the continuous articulated band of steel track shoes, rubber-bushed pins, and track pads that encircles the road wheels, idler wheel, and drive sprocket.
track system.what_it_does: It distributes vehicle gross combat weight across low ground contact pressure, converts drive sprocket rotational torque into linear tractive tractive effort across cross-country terrain, and provides continuous traction.
track system.where_it_fits: Vehicle Running Gear and Mobility Subsystem, mounted along the lower hull flanks outside the torsion bar suspension stations.
explicit_relationships: Track engages with the drive sprocket teeth to transmit automotive torque.
Track runs under the suspension road wheels connected to the torsion bar stations.
track system.general_context_note: Suspension station and torsion bar interface documented directly in SOP; track envelope parameters are standard armoured vehicle engineering context.

engine alignment.what_it_is: Engine alignment is the precision mechanical spatial and coaxial positioning of the V12 diesel engine crankshaft output flange relative to the transmission input shaft.
engine alignment.what_it_does: It eliminates parallel radial offset and angular face misalignment, preventing catastrophic driveline vibration, premature bearing destruction, flexible coupling shear, and power transmission failure.
engine alignment.where_it_fits: Engine Bay Compartment between the V12 Powerpack and the cross-drive hydromechanical transmission.
explicit_relationships: Engine output flange couples to transmission input flange via calibrated elastomeric coupling.
Precision shim packs under engine hydromounts adjust vertical and lateral alignment.
engine alignment.general_context_note: Alignment procedures, dial indicator radial/axial tolerances, and shimming steps are directly stated in the Engine Alignment SOP.
